primitives.verbatim_quote: When the blocking is released we feel as if an inward spring were let loose, and this is the additional impulse or fiat upon which the act effectively succeeds.

primitives.breakdown_regime: t → 0 implies instantaneous actuation; F_b → ∞ implies complete inhibition.

primitives.name: Neural Force Balance
primitives.verbatim_quote: A waking man's behavior is thus at all times the resultant of two opposing neural forces.
primitives.assumptions: Behavioral output R = F_e - F_i; both forces vary continuously in time and space.
primitives.breakdown_regime: F_e ≈ F_i implies minimal motion; F_e >> F_i implies strong execution.

layer2.mapping: Represents the core mechanism of voluntary control through opposing neural fields. GSI uses it to model decision confidence in action selection. GSE applies it to simulate agent conflict resolution.
layer2.telemetry: Differential neural activity between excitation and inhibition regions

The foundational principle of ideomotor action posits that movement arises immediately from feeling, forming a direct causal link between affective state and motor output. This is formalized through a dual-force model where neural excitation and inhibition interact dynamically. Blocking-release dynamics introduce a temporal component, creating a delayed but potentiated motor impulse. The system operates under a continuous feedback loop of neural currents, where inhibition can suppress action while excitation promotes it. These principles form a coherent mathematical structure: F(t) = F_e(t) - F_i(t), where F(t) represents net motor force at time t. The system exhibits bistability—either fully inhibited or activated—depending on the relative strength of competing neural inputs. This leads to a phase transition model of action initiation, where small perturbations in F_e or F_i can trigger large-scale behavioral shifts. The breakdown regime occurs when either force approaches zero or infinity, indicating loss of control or saturation of the system. The derived kernel allows for probabilistic modeling of action outcomes based on neural state distributions.
